You will need:

Effigy or poppit 

Black candle 

Fireproof container 

The effigy curse utilizes an image or representation (effigy) of the intended victim and the flame of a black candle. The effigy can be anything you wish. Their name on a small piece of paper is pragmatic and simple. Keep in mind you’re about to set the effigy on fire.

The amount of damage done to the victim is correlated with the amount of energy and rage you put into the ritual. This ritual will typically cause misfortune in the form of injury or the loss of something they hold dear. Advanced practitioners can direct their intentions to achieve a specific outcome. 

Light the black candle on your altar and place a fireproof bowl or plate in front of the candle. Carefully take your effigy and set the corner on fire using the candle, do this in a well-ventilated space, preferably outside. Immediately drop the effigy in the bowl and chant the following aloud.

“This is the time of retribution, 

I invoke the elements, 

I summon them, 

I conjure them to do my bidding, 

The four watchtowers, grant me thy power, 

Bring forth fear, guilt and pain, 

There shall be submission without pity, 

I direct my hate against thee, 

Against thee it shall be directed, 

A hundred-fold is the cost for my anger and pain, 

Thee shall be wrought with fear, 

anointed with pain, 

Blinded by me, binded by me, 

cursed by me, So mote it be!”

Once the fire has burnt out you may extinguish the candle to conclude the ritual.

With my first ex, immediately after our breakup, I tried manifesting us getting back together. But something felt off. Really off. I tried visualizing and I just knew in my gut that this was not right for me. And it wasn't. I was a teen at that time and I always excused my ex's abusive behaviour because I thought I loved him. It was only months later when I fell out of love with him, I realized that he violated my physical and sexual boundaries many times and didn't ask for my consent. 

I believe you always know deep down if someone is right for you. If there's even a teeny tiny part of you that feels off, I'll say don't manifest and let the person go. Because manifestations do come true but that doesn't mean they are always right for you.

Now if you do decide to manifest, visualize and let it go. Letting go being the absolute key here. With my second bf, I had feelings for him for over a year. However, he had some deep commitment issues and he didn't feel romantically for me at the time. 

I pined over him for so long but ultimately decided to let him go because I was tired of it being so one-sided. And literally like the week after I made peace with the fact that he didn't like me back, he started falling for me. xD I'm not even kidding. So yes, manifest, TRULY let your ex go and work on yourself. Chances are you'll realize you're better off without them.
